paragraphs: I'm a Software Engineer with a Master's in Software Engineering from the University of Maryland (May 2026). I bring 2 years of prior enterprise experience from Capgemini Technology Services (Oct 2022 – Sep 2024), where I engineered integration systems for MUFG Bank within a 100+ member global engineering organization supporting a platform processing over $100M in daily transactions.

My engineering philosophy sits at the intersection of enterprise rigor and modern product velocity. I build reliable, scalable full-stack applications with Java, Python, TypeScript, and Next.js, and I integrate generative AI (Gemini, Llama3) into real products — not just prototypes.
I take ownership from the database schema to the deployment pipeline. Most recently that means Huddle, a production geospatial platform I designed, built, and launched solo.

experience.role: Software Engineer → Senior Software Engineer, Enterprise Integration
bullets: Delivered 20+ production RESTful services and integration pipelines within a 100+ member global engineering organization supporting MUFG Bank's transaction platform processing $100M+ daily, by designing Java-based middleware on IBM Integration Bus.
Reduced post-deployment incidents 25% by building event-driven middleware with structured logging and monitoring across distributed services using WebSphere MQ.
Cut feature integration time 30% across 5 application teams by architecting automated build-test-deploy CI/CD pipelines with Jenkins and JFrog Artifactory.

projects.title: Huddle - Community Operating System
projects.shortDesc: Launched a production hyperlocal event-discovery platform with live campus users. Prevented race conditions across 500+ events under concurrent load by engineering transactional Firestore writes. Cut redundant API calls 90% via viewport debouncing.
projects.problem: Huddle began with a problem I lived every day at UMD — the chaos of discovering and organizing local campus events.
projects.solution: What started as a small MVP evolved, through mentorship from the Dingman Center Hatchery program, into a scalable hyperlocal platform. We utilized Next.js 15, TypeScript, and Firebase to create real-time discoverability.
projects.impact: Grew to successfully track 500+ events, acting as the centralized hub for community engagement on campus.

projects.title: ClassNest - AI-Powered Learning Management System
projects.shortDesc: Enforced 90% test coverage via Test-Driven Development (Django/React). Automated PDF-to-quiz conversion by engineering an LLM pipeline with Llama3 via Groq API.
projects.problem: Educators often spend significant manual effort creating engaging and relevant learning materials. The challenge was to design a system that could automate content creation and provide a scalable, multi-user learning environment.
projects.solution: I led the development of a full-featured LMS using a Django MVT backend and a React frontend. The core innovation was an AI-driven quiz generation module using the Groq API and Llama3 LLM, which automatically converts uploaded PDF documents into interactive quizzes. The system also features secure, role-based access control for administrators, educators, and students.
projects.impact: This system significantly enhances educator efficiency by automating content creation. The AI-powered features provide a more dynamic and adaptive learning experience for students, directly addressing the need for modern, intelligent educational tools.

projects.title: IoT Smart Health Monitoring System
projects.shortDesc: IoT-based system for real-time remote patient health monitoring and alerts.
projects.problem: Healthcare providers require a reliable method to monitor patients' vital signs remotely to provide timely care, especially for those with chronic conditions or in post-operative recovery.
projects.solution: As team lead, I architected an IoT-based system that uses Arduino and Raspberry Pi to collect real-time patient data (heart rate, temperature, oxygen levels) from various sensors. I then developed a responsive web interface to display this data clearly, allowing for remote monitoring by medical professionals.
projects.impact: The system successfully demonstrated a viable solution for improving remote healthcare delivery. It ensures continuous monitoring and enables faster interventions, bridging the communication gap between patients and doctors.

projects.title: GitHub Issues & Contributor Analysis
projects.shortDesc: Data analysis and visualization of open-source project health and contributor trends.
projects.problem: Large open-source projects like 'Poetry' struggle to understand contributor engagement trends and identify bottlenecks in issue resolution, which can slow down development and discourage new contributors.
projects.solution: I performed a comprehensive data analysis on the Poetry project's GitHub repository. Using Python, Pandas, and Matplotlib, I processed and visualized issue data to reveal patterns in contributor engagement and project responsiveness. I also developed unit tests to ensure the reliability of the data processing workflow.
projects.impact: My analysis provided actionable insights into the project's health, identifying key areas for improving community management and issue triage. The visualizations made complex data easily understandable for project maintainers.

projects.title: Real-Time Utility Consumption Monitor
projects.shortDesc: IoT and Django web app for real-time tracking and visualization of utility usage.
projects.problem: Households often lack real-time visibility into their electricity and water usage, making it difficult to manage consumption, identify waste, and control costs effectively.
projects.solution: I designed and built a complete IoT solution, from hardware to software. Using Arduino and Raspberry Pi, I created a custom energy meter to capture real-time data. This data was then sent to a Django web application I developed, which provided users with a friendly interface to track and visualize their consumption patterns over time.
projects.impact: The web app empowered users with immediate feedback on their utility usage, enabling them to make informed decisions to conserve resources and reduce their monthly bills.

huddleShowcase.title: Huddle: Discover. Create. Connect.
paragraphs: Huddle began with a problem I lived every day at UMD — the chaos of discovering and organizing local campus events. What started as a small MVP evolved, through mentorship from the Dingman Center Hatchery program, into a scalable hyperlocal platform designed to be the "operating system for local communities."

The initial spark came from the frustration of organizing pickup cricket games, but this quickly pivoted into a generalized, dynamic map view. The core challenge became re-architecting the entire application—from the Firestore data model to the UI components—to scale across different event types while preserving its signature speed and "glassmorphism" aesthetic.

features.title: Scalable Serverless Backend
features.desc: Built on a modern, serverless architecture using Next.js 15 API Routes and Firebase for security and performance at scale.

features.title: Dynamic, Real-Time Map View
features.desc: Utilizes the Google Maps Platform with custom, cloud-based styling to serve as the central hub for discovering local events in real-time.

features.title: AI-Assisted Event Creation
features.desc: Features an intuitive, multi-step modal that integrates the Google Gemini API to help organizers generate catchy, context-aware titles and descriptions.

features.title: Secure Authentication & Community Tools
features.desc: A complete authentication system with user profiles, a trust-building "check-in" system, and event-specific real-time chat.
